sections.html:
Property tax in Ben Hill County runs through a pair of offices. Bills and payments go through the Tax Commissioner, 324 East Pine Street, Fitzgerald. What a property is worth is the Board of Tax Assessors' call. The commissioner's number is (229) 426-5144, answered on weekdays, and the counter stays staffed until half past four. The assessors are at (229) 426-5147.

A payment, a lien or a wrong mailing address is a commissioner matter. A value, a homestead file or an exemption belongs with the assessors. Appraisers keep inspecting properties, stop at every parcel with a building permit, and look for a current decal on each mobile home.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, receipts, liens, online payments
  • Board of Tax Assessors: value, returns, exemptions, notices of assessment
  • Clerk of Superior Court: your warranty deed copy, from the courthouse deed room

sections.h2: Ben Hill County at a glance
sections.html:
This is a small south Georgia county. Fitzgerald is its only city and also the seat. The population slipped from 17,194 at the 2020 census to an estimate of 17,099 for 2025. A typical home is valued at $112,700 while a typical household earns $41,758, so a tax bill takes a bigger bite here than in a pricier market.

Housing totals 8,166 units in 2025, and owners occupy 63.3 percent. Middle gross rent is $688 a month and the average commute is only 16.8 minutes. Buyers at these price levels watch every dollar, so clear any tax question before you list.

Land, houses and business personal property are normally due December 1. Georgia's default is December 20 and counties are allowed to move it, which is why the day on your own statement is the one to follow. Mobile homes are due April 1, and a call to the office will confirm that for your account.

Interest on a late account is 1% a month. Once 90 days go by, a one-time 10% penalty applies, though a homesteaded parcel owing under $500 escapes it. Past 90 days the balance can turn into a FiFa lien in the records of the Clerk of Superior Court, where credit bureaus may pick it up, and the commissioner may then levy on the parcel.

Statements go to the owner and not to the lender. If a mortgage escrow pays your tax, pass the bill along or confirm the servicer is handling it.

Cash and checks cost nothing extra at the counter, and a check in the mail works too. The county's GovtWindow portal takes online payments, and PayPal and cards are offered only on the website. Every online method adds a convenience charge that shows before you confirm, so you can back out and pay by check.

  • In person: 324 East Pine Street, Fitzgerald, Georgia 31750
  • By phone for questions: (229) 426-5144
  • Portal help line: (877) 575-7233

To qualify you must own the home and live in it on January 1, and the assessors need your application before April 1. It renews each year as long as you stay. After a move you apply again for the new address, and a filing that comes in late only shifts the benefit to the following year.

Owners who turn 62 can apply for an added exemption. Business inventory may qualify for a freeport exemption in places where local voters approved one. Local legislation can raise the base amounts, so call the assessors for the dollar figure that applies to you.

If you are selling, your exemption does not travel with the house. The buyer files a new application, and telling their agent early avoids a surprise on the first bill.

sections.h2: How values are set and challenged
sections.html:
Through winter and early spring, until April 1, you may file a return that names your own value. When the board disagrees, it mails a notice showing its figure. Taxable value is 40% of market value, and each mill brings in one dollar per $1,000 of that taxable value.

You have 45 days from the notice date to appeal, and the case goes either to the county Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. Still unhappy? Deliver written notice to the assessors and take it to superior court. A claim for tax charged by mistake must be made within three years of payment.

Find out the balance and who is billed before you sign anything. The statement carries the January 1 owner, so it can show your name even if the buyer takes the deed later in the year. Request a printed balance from the commissioner, and have the closing agent explain how that year is divided with the buyer.

Title cannot pass cleanly while a lien stands. Most sellers pay it from the sale money, and the commissioner's payoff figure is the amount to wire. Repairs the house needs do not block a sale while taxes are owed, which is one reason some owners pick a cash buyer who accepts the house as it is.

At the counter on East Pine Street, bring your deed or parcel number, your latest statement and any lien notice. Ask for the payoff in writing with its good-through date, because interest builds each month.

Georgia treats mobile and modular homes as personal property. Each year the owner files a return and gets a location permit, and the year's tax must be paid in full before that permit is issued. April 1 is the due date for that account, so confirm the date on yours with the commissioner.

Assessors look for a current decal when they inspect. If you sell one, the next owner takes over the paperwork trail, so pay the tax and settle the permit before the handoff and keep the paid receipt.

Owners who moved without updating an address should ask the assessors whether mail came back undelivered, so future notices reach the right place. A missed notice does not stop the 45-day appeal clock.

faqs.q: When is real estate tax due in Ben Hill County?
faqs.a: Most bills are due December 1, but the date printed on your statement controls. Call (229) 426-5144 to confirm.

faqs.q: What does a late Ben Hill County payment cost?
faqs.a: Interest runs 1% per month, and a 10% penalty is added after 90 days. Homesteaded property with a liability under $500 skips the penalty.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for homestead exemption in Ben Hill County?
faqs.a: Apply with the Tax Assessor, and make sure the paperwork arrives before April 1. You must own the home and live there on January 1.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window in Ben Hill County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date. Appeals go to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, with superior court after that.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Ben Hill County taxes without a fee?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying cash or check at the counter or mailing a check costs nothing extra, while online payments add a convenience charge.
